---
title: The shape of a page
subtitle: Prose, hierarchy, and the details between them.
---

## A comfortable measure

The first obligation of a page is to be read. A comfortable line, a generous
margin, and an unhurried rhythm do much of the work. Consistency makes the
details useful: the space above a heading, the weight of a rule, the way a
link sits inside a sentence.

This paragraph contains *emphasis*, **a stronger point**, and an
[ordinary link](code.qmd). An expression such as `library.find()` has a
different voice. Numbers 0123456789, “quotation marks,” and an em dash — all
belong to the same typographic system.

### A smaller thought

A heading helps the reader skim and settle back into the text.

1. Start with a concrete question or a small example.
2. Explain enough for the reader to understand the decision.
3. Leave a useful route to the next idea.

> Read a little, think a little, and keep something worth returning to.

::: {.callout-tip}
## A useful aside
A quieter detail can sit in its own place without interrupting the argument.
